newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel president apologises for gay-bashing.
newsitem.headline: Israel president apologises for gay-bashing.

text.p: Israeli President Ezer Weizman met on Monday with gay and lesbian leaders and apologised for publicly deriding homosexuality as "abnormal".
"The president says that he must express sorrow for any act or comment that causes public humiliation or can be interpreted as such," his spokesman Arieh Shumer told reporters after the meeting.
"It is necessary to guard the honour, rights and welfare of all the citizens of the state of Israel," Shumer added.
Weizman, whose presidential role is largely symbolic, took aim at homosexuals during a speech last week to Israeli high school students in the northern city of Haifa.

"(Homosexuality) is abnormal from a social point of view. I don't like it. What the public decides to do with (homosexuals), it will decide through laws," Weizman said, drawing applause from students.
The cheers turned to giggles as Weizman used an inflection to deride homosexuality.
"It has become 'nice'," the president said, his voice rising in tone. He repeated the word 'nice' in an even higher pitch.
Rabbis lauded Weizman but hundreds of Israeli rights activists protested outside the president's Jerusalem home on Saturday to demand his resignation.
Gay leaders expressed satisfaction with Weizman's apology.

"Although it is difficult for Ezer, given his character, to say I am sorry, I apologise, he did the maximum so that we would understand in the meeting that he indeed made a mistake," activist Adir Steiner told reporters.
